runs.text: denotes a family of indefinite integrals indexed by the nonnegative integer n.
A reduction formula expresses an indexed integral in terms of a lower-index member, so repeated application must terminate at stated base cases.
This recurrence follows from integration by parts and the Pythagorean identity. For definite integrals, derive or use the corresponding recurrence with boundary terms evaluated before iterating.

items.text: Here n is an integer at least 2; the parity of n determines which base case is reached.
Constants of integration need not be carried at every recursive step; add one constant to the final antiderivative.
Different integral families have different boundary terms and recurrences, so derive rather than transplant a formula.
A recurrence without base cases does not finish the computation.
Check whether the formula is for an indefinite integral or a particular definite interval.
